venue_analysis.campus_green_bean_cafe: cafe, $, peanut_free, healthy; reviews mention grain bowls, salads, light food, peanuts kept out of the kitchen. Meets every constraint.
venue_analysis.campus_nutty_mug: cafe, $, healthy, but NOT peanut_free; review says peanut butter in smoothies and crushed nuts on bowls. Allergy deal-breaker.
venue_analysis.campus_griddle_house: cafe, $, peanut_free, but no healthy tag; reviews describe butter-soaked, fried, greasy food. Misses the not-greasy and fresh preferences (about -1 to -2 stars).
venue_analysis.campus_sprout_lounge: cafe, peanut_free, healthy, but $$; one tier over budget (-1 star).

notes: Fair, clean puzzle. Each decoy fails exactly one dimension (allergy, healthy/grease, budget), which is good design. The Nutty Mug trap works: the registry leaves out peanut_free and the review confirms it, while Maya's line about cafes sneaking peanut butter into smoothies nudges the player to check. The cafe constraint does not separate the options, since all four are cafes. Small points: 'no greasy' and 'something fresh' may count as one preference or two, which only changes Griddle House's score, not the answer. The venue name 'Nutty Mug' gives the trap away, which makes it a bit obvious. I made the pick from the tags and reviews, not the name. Brooke asks for sandwiches but no venue mentions them; it doesn't affect anything. No contradictions found.
